Priya (support): FYI customer 'AcmeHealth' reporting mass 403s after a scheduled key rotation ~16:02 UTC. They say only traffic from edge cluster eu-west is affected. Errors look like 'invalid_api_key' and 'permission denied'.
Samir (sre): Can you paste the exact error they see? tenant id / request id? also which auth path - api key, service account, or Vault-wrapped key?
Priya (support): They pasted this snip from their app logs: ```2026-11-03T16:03:11Z ERROR auth failed request_id=abc123 status=403 reason="invalid_api_key" detail="signature mismatch"``` They mention we rotated the API keys via the console and rotated the KMS envelope keys yesterday. Their pods mount secrets via a sidecar that reads K8s secrets into env vars.
Jill (devex): Sidecar env var reloading is a known race with short-lived tokens. Did the sidecar pick up the new secret? If the secret was updated but the sidecar holds old in-memory token, it will keep calling with old creds -> 403.
Priya (support): Customer says some pods recovered after a restart, but ~40% of requests kept failing and they want a fast mitigation.
Samir (sre): Ok quick triage checklist: 1) confirm which pods still failing, 2) check kube secret value hash vs sidecar cache, 3) check Vault/KMS decrypt errors in our logs. Priya can you ask for `kubectl get pods -o wide` and the sidecar logs for failing pods?
Priya (support): Sent commands to customer. They returned sidecar logs (redacted): ```2026-11-03T16:04:05Z sidecar INFO loading secret from /var/run/secrets/sa-token 2026-11-03T16:04:05Z sidecar WARN token ttl expired, attempting rewrap 2026-11-03T16:04:06Z sidecar ERROR KMS decrypt failed: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc="key not found or wrong key_version" 2026-11-03T16:04:06Z http ERROR upstream auth failed status=403"```
Liam (infra): That KMS error stands out: "key not found or wrong key_version" — sounds like the envelope/key version the sidecar used was rotated and old versions were disabled before all pods finished rewrapping. We had a short grace window on rewrap -> some pods try to decrypt with old version.
Samir (sre): Agreed. Short-term mitigation: force the sidecar to reload secrets or restart the pod so it fetches the new wrapped token. Commands: ```kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/<edge-deployment> # rolling restart``` or per-pod: ```kubectl delete pod <pod-name> -n prod```
Jill (devex): If they can't restart, sidecar exposes a reload endpoint in v0.8+: `POST /internal/reload-secrets` on 127.0.0.1:8060. Hitting that will make it re-fetch the secret and try decrypt again.
Priya (support): Customer tried `kubectl delete pod` for a few failing pods and reports immediate recovery for those pods. But some orgs can't do restarts during peak. What's a safer fix?
Liam (infra): Longer fix: update our KMS/Vault rotation policy to keep previous key versions enabled for a longer grace window (we currently disable after 5m). Also ensure Vault rewrap job waits for in-flight pods to refresh if using short TTLs. Suggest bump to 30m for envelope grace for clusters with sidecar env propagation.
Samir (sre): Also add a fallback in the sidecar: if decrypt returns key_version_mismatch, try listing latest key versions and attempt rewrap against them, or expose a retry loop with exponential backoff. Right now it errors immediately.
Jill (devex): Actionable steps for support now: 1) Ask customer to roll the edge deployment a few pods at a time, or call the sidecar reload endpoint if restarts are restricted. 2) Confirm the KMS key version in our logs matches the one in their wrapped token. 3) We'll open an infra ticket to extend the rewrap grace window and add better logging on key_version mismatches.
Priya (support): I've documented the repro & mitigation to send to the customer: - Cause: race between KMS envelope key rotation and sidecar in-memory token refresh. - Short-term: restart pods or call POST /internal/reload-secrets on sidecar. - Mid-term: infra to increase grace window + sidecar retry work.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-11-03-779 (priority P2) assigned to eng-runtime.
Liam (infra): I'll own the infra ticket. Quick note: check Vault audit around `2026-11-03T16:02` for `transit/decrypt` calls returning 404/PermissionDenied to see which key_version was requested.
Samir (sre): Also add to postmortem: customer-facing mitigation time, number of affected pods, whether any requests were rate-limited during the event.
Priya (support): I'll follow up with the customer with step-by-step commands and ask them to confirm when all pods show healthy. I'll also attach the sidecar log snippet and our suggested restart schedule.
Jill (devex): Extra reminder for devs: make the sidecar watch the projected token file instead of only reading at startup; or at least implement `SIGHUP`/`POST /internal/reload-secrets`. Little changes avoid this blast radius.
Priya (support): Customer confirmed 90% recovery after rolling restart; they schedule a maintenance window for full rollout. They asked if we can provide a KB on safe rotation for env-var mounted secrets. I'll open a docs ticket.
Samir (sre): Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: - infra to update rotation grace window (Liam) - devex to add reload ergonomics (Jill) - support to send KB + customer steps (Priya).
Priya (support): Marking thread resolved for now. Customer will reopen if anything else pops. :white_check_mark:
